intro: Lesson 55: Co-interior angles and multi-step angle problems. To understand how co-interior angles and chains of angle facts solve multi-step parallel-line problems

model.title: Between parallel lines, on the same side of the transversal, the angles are 70° and y. Find y.

A triangle has its top vertex on the upper of two parallel lines and its base on the lower line. At the top vertex its sides make angles of 50° (left) and 60° (right) with the upper line. Find the triangle's angles.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Left base angle = 50° (alternate angles are equal)

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Right base angle = 60° (alternate angles are equal)

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Top angle = 180 - 50 - 60 = 70° (angles on a straight line)

questions.q: Co-interior angles are 115° and y. Find y.
questions.model: Co-interior angles add up to 180°. y = 180 - 115 = 65°.

questions.q: Alternate angles are (4x - 15)° and (2x + 25)°. Find x.
Name the angles between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal.

(a) an angle co-interior with 98° (b) a is alternate to 47° and b lies on a straight line with a (c) co-interior angles are 3p° and 2p°: find p (d) a triangle has its top vertex on the upper parallel line, where its sides make angles of 38° and 71° with that line: find the triangle's three angles
questions.model: (c) Co-interior angles add up to 180°: 3p + 2p = 180, 5p = 180, p = 36. (d) Base angles 38° and 71° (alternate angles); top angle 180 - 38 - 71 = 71°.

questions.q: Prove that opposite angles of a parallelogram ABCD are equal.
questions.a: A + B = 180 (co-interior, AD ∥ BC) and B + C = 180 (co-interior, AB ∥ DC), so A = C.

questions.q: A bent line runs between two parallel lines. It makes 40° with the top line and 30° with the bottom line (both measured on the left). Find the angle at the bend.
questions.a: 70°: draw a third parallel line through the bend; alternate angles give 40° + 30°.

questions.q: Big question: how can you find an angle that seems unlinked?
questions.a: Chain facts: find an unlabelled angle with one fact, then use it with the next, naming each fact.
